renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: contiguity_scatter
  title: Contiguity of each assembly
  description: |-
    Each point is an assembly: its number of sequences on the horizontal axis and its N50 on the vertical axis, sized by its total length and coloured by the share of N bases. It answers which assemblies are chromosome-level and which are fragmented drafts.
    How to read: the upper left corner holds few, long sequences, the signature of a chromosome-level assembly. Points at the lower right are fragmented, and long alignments between genomes cannot span their breaks. A dark point carries many N bases, which are gaps that cannot align.
    Note: N50 is the sequence length at which half of the assembly is reached, longest first, and the assembly-scan README states no quality cut-off, so none is drawn.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median N50 of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut- off of assembly-scan.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rpetit3/assembly-scan/master/README.md and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N50,_L50,_and_related_statistics
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    color_col: n_pct
    log_x: true
    log_y: true
    x_title: Sequences in the assembly
    y_title: N50 (bp)
    top_n_labels: 8
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: contigs
    y: n50
    label: genome
    size: total_length

- component: figure
  title: GC content per assembly
  description: |-
    Each bar is an assembly, with its GC content as a percentage of its bases. It answers whether the assemblies have a similar base composition.
    How to read: bars of similar height are expected for closely related genomes. An assembly far from the rest may be a different species, or may be contaminated or built from another source.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median GC content of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of assembly-scan.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rpetit3/assembly-scan/master/README.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: genome
    y: gc_pct
    labels:
      genome: Assembly
      gc_pct: GC content (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: gc_pct

- component: card
  id: assembly_n50
  title: Assembly N50
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median N50 of the assemblies, the length of the sequence at which half of the assembly is reached when sorted longest first, with the lowest and highest values. It answers how contiguous the assemblies are.
    How to read: a high N50 means long sequences, up to chromosome scale. A low N50 beside a large sequence count marks a fragmented draft.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rpetit3/assembly-scan/master/README.md and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N50,_L50,_and_related_statistics
  column: n50
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: grid
  caption: median, with the shortest and longest
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: assembly_length
  title: Assembly length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median total length of the assemblies in base pairs, runs of N included, with the smallest and largest. It answers how large the genomes are.
    How to read: assemblies of related species should be of similar length. A much smaller assembly is probably incomplete, and a larger one may hold duplicated or contaminating sequence.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rpetit3/assembly-scan/master/README.md
  column: total_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: grid
  caption: median, with the smallest and largest

- component: card
  id: assembly_large_share
  title: Sequences over 1 Mb
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of an assembly's sequences that are longer than 1 Mb, and the histogram shows how the assemblies distribute. It answers how many assemblies are built from megabase-scale sequences.
    How to read: chromosome-level assemblies pile near 100 percent and fragmented ones near 0, so two humps mean two kinds of assembly.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rpetit3/assembly-scan/master/README.md
  column: contigs_over_1mb_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: share of sequences over 1 Mb, per assembly

- component: card
  id: assembly_gc
  title: GC content
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median GC content of the assemblies as a percentage, and the box shows the spread. It answers how similar the base composition is across assemblies.
    How to read: a narrow box means related genomes. An outlier assembly may be a different organism or contaminated.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rpetit3/assembly-scan/master/README.md
  column: gc_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  id: assembly_contigs
  title: Sequences per assembly
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of sequences (contigs or scaffolds) in an assembly, with the fewest and the most. It answers how fragmented the assemblies are.
    How to read: a count close to the number of chromosomes means a near-complete assembly. Hundreds or thousands of sequences mean a draft.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rpetit3/assembly-scan/master/README.md
  column: contigs
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: grid
  caption: median, with the fewest and the most

- component: interactive
  title: N50 range
  description: Filters the tiles to assemblies whose N50 falls inside the chosen range.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: n50

- component: table
  title: Assembly statistics table
  description: |-
    Each row is an assembly with its sequence count, total, median and longest length, N50 and L50, GC and N content, and the sequences past 1 kb, 10 kb, 100 kb and 1 Mb. It answers the exact numbers behind every tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by N50 to rank the assemblies by contiguity.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rpetit3/assembly-scan/master/README.md
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: genome
